biography: Rodolfo Pousa's journey began not on asphalt, but on the dusty dirt tracks of rural Brazil. Growing up in a small farming community, his first taste of speed came from piloting his grandfather's old pickup truck around the fields – a skill he honed with daring abandon. He transitioned to karting at 18, self-taught and fiercely competitive, quickly making a name for himself in regional championships. His breakthrough came during a particularly rainy race in São Paulo, where his uncanny car control in treacherous conditions caught the eye of a Copa Uno team owner. Since then, Pousa has become a mainstay in the Copa Uno series, known for his consistent performance and relentless pursuit of improvement. While he hasn't yet clinched a championship title, he remains a formidable contender, a testament to his raw talent and unwavering dedication, now entering what many consider his peak years.
drivingStyle: Pousa is a study in calculated aggression. He doesn't often make flashy, high-risk moves, but he's incredibly consistent and precise. He excels at tire management, often able to push harder for longer than his competitors. His cornering style is characterized by a late braking technique, allowing him to carry significant speed through the apex. He's known for his ability to maintain composure under pressure, rarely cracking even in the most intense racing situations. This makes him a particularly dangerous opponent in endurance races.

rivalries.reason: A fierce on-track battle during the 2021 Interlagos race resulted in a controversial collision, leading to a heated exchange of words and a lingering animosity.
Almeida, a veteran driver, has frequently accused Pousa of overly aggressive blocking tactics, leading to several tense moments both on and off the track.
Costa, a young prodigy, represents the new generation of racing talent. Pousa views him as a threat to his established position, and there's a palpable tension whenever they share the track.

quirks: Always wears the same faded blue wristband, a gift from his grandfather, during every race.
Refuses to eat any food containing tomatoes on race days.
Listens to a specific Brazilian folk song on repeat in the hour leading up to a race, claiming it helps him focus.
famousQuote: "The track doesn't care about your name or your reputation. It only respects those who are willing to push themselves to the limit, and beyond."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2020 Rio de Janeiro Copa Uno race in dominant fashion, overcoming a poor qualifying position to take the lead and hold it for the majority of the race.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the 2019 São Paulo championship decider due to a mechanical failure while leading, costing him his best chance at the championship title.
